thread:
dmitri: Ran a perfetto + nvprof sweep after the batching heuristic change (dynamic window 16->32). Seeing periodic GPU allocator spikes that align with KV-cache eviction windows. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:

caro: can you grab the kernel timeline + allocation stack for one of the spikes? a screenshot of the flame/track helps a lot :thinking:

dmitri: uploaded timeline + short log. The pattern is: burst of small CUDA allocations (~5-20KB) for ~200ms, then a couple large cudaMalloc calls (~several MB) during eviction. nsys cmd I used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output batcher_eviction`

--- log excerpt ---
[2026-03-15 14:02:41] batcher: window=32 active=290 queued=12
[2026-03-15 14:02:41] kvcache: evicting 4 entries, epoch=128
[2026-03-15 14:02:41] cudaMalloc 1: 8388608 bytes (8 MB) latency=2.1ms
[2026-03-15 14:02:41] cudaMalloc 2: 4194304 bytes (4 MB) latency=1.8ms
[2026-03-15 14:02:41] small allocs x ~120: avg 0.03ms each
--- end ---

ben: interesting — smells like fragmentation + fallback to system allocator when arena can't satisfy mixed small+large pattern. do we have the allocator "growth" and "max-block" settings? also share the jemalloc-like stats if available

dmitri: here's allocator dump from our internal pool at that moment:
```
arena_total: 256MB
arena_used: 198MB
free_chunks: 34
largest_free: 2.5MB
internal_frag: 22%
fallback_alloc_count: 3
```

elaine: kernel selection note: after the heuristic change we start choosing the fp16-int8 hybrid conv kernels which allocate transient workspace buffers for fusion; those workspaces are fairly large and short-lived. coupling that with KV eviction means we get interleaved alloc patterns. could be the root cause

caro: try two quick experiments:
1) force the allocator to prefer bigger blocks (grow factor 1.5 -> 2.5) and retest
2) disable parallel eviction (serialize evict) to see if peak goes away

ben: commands to repro profile (if anyone wants to run locally):
```
# reproduce a 30s window with heavy batching
NSYS_OUT=./out nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=cudaAPI --duration 30 --output out_eviction
python -m scripts/run_bench --batcher-window=32 --kv-evict-rate=high
```

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T14:01:30 started on infra/batchers (rollout-id: r-77f9) :rocket:

dmitri: ran (1) and (2):
- increasing grow factor reduced fallback_alloc_count to 0 and lowered largest single cudaMalloc from 8MB -> 2.6MB. peak GPU resident decreased by ~110MB.
- serializing eviction eliminated the synchronized burst but increased tail latency for cold lookups (tradeoff obvious)

caro: good signal. we probably want smarter reuse: 1) pre-reserve a small slab for eviction-time large buffers, 2) tighten the arena split threshold so small allocs don't fragment big free ranges. i'll sketch config

caro: config snippet to try (runtime JSON):
```
{"gpu_allocator": {"grow_factor": "2.0", "slab_reserve_mb": "64", "split_threshold_kb": "512"}}
```

elaine: also add NVTX annotations around eviction + kernel selection to make the perfetto tracks filterable. then we can correlate which kernel families are allocating workspaces and how big

ben: +1. if we add a tiny histogram of cudaMalloc sizes into our metrics, we can alert on unexpected tails (eg >1MB rate spikes)

dmitri: did a follow-up run with the slab_reserve and split_threshold applied. result: eviction still happens but no system cudaMalloc observed; fragmentation dropped to 9%. attaching perfetto diff (two traces): https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 vs https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd5678 :thumbsup:

elaine: awesome. next steps:
- add NVTX ranges on kernel selection branch and eviction start/end (action: @dmitri)
- bake the slab_reserve into a canary config for Dedicated (action: @caro)
- emit cudaMalloc size histogram metric (action: @ben)

dmitri: will add NVTX tags and push a quick run tomorrow morning. thanks all! :party_parrot:
